title: Derived internal-Hom adjunction on a scheme
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let K, L, M be objects of D(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category]. Write K\otimes^L L for the derived tensor product, represented by \operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal P^\bullet\otimes_{O_X}\mathcal L^\bullet) [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] for a K-flat complex \mathcal P^\bullet with a quasi-isomorphism \mathcal P^\bullet\to K [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and a complex \mathcal L^\bullet representing L, and R\mathcal Hom for the derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then there is a canonical bijection, functorial in K, L, and M, Hom_{D(O_X)}(K,R\mathcal Hom(L,M))\cong Hom_{D(O_X)}(K\otimes^L L,M). Moreover there is a canonical isomorphism K\otimes^L L\cong L\otimes^L K, functorial in K and L, so that also Hom_{D(O_X)}(K,R\mathcal Hom(L,M))\cong Hom_{D(O_X)}(L\otimes^L K,M), functorial in K, L, and M.

proof.text: Use the existence theorem of [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-bijection] to obtain e and its naturality in all three variables. Its representative normalization is stronger than needed here.

Obtain the natural symmetry s of the shared derived tensor from [lem-sc-scheme-derived-tensor-symmetry]. Define e′ by composing e with precomposition by s inverse, using Iso.homCongr. This is an equivalence.

The defining precomposition equation is immediate. Cancel s.hom in its naturality square to obtain s(K′,L′).inv composed with (a tensor b) equals (b tensor a) composed with s(K,L).inv. Combine this with naturality of e and associativity to prove the final naturality equation.
